pr_title: Add new filter BIO BIO_f_readbuffer() that allows buffering a stdin file into memory.
pr_body:
Required so that BIO_tell() and BIO_seek() work with stdin inside the decoder.
    
Fixes #13185
Fixes #13352
    
This works for stdin taken from input redirection (command < file) and stdin via pipe (cat file | command).
(Note that Input redirection uses BIO_gets()).
    
This BIO is for reading purposes only.

pr_comments: As this is really not restricted to use with stdin should it be called something like BIO_f_readbuffer()?

> As this is really not restricted to use with stdin should it be called something like BIO_f_readbuffer()?

Thanks for the name..
Rebased to fix up the names in the commit message. The last 2 commits contain updates related to the review comments.

I am still concerned about one thing - this technically is an API break, isn't it? Or do the BIO APIs that read keys and certs that were present in 1.1.1 work still with unseekable BIOs without the BIO_f_readbuffer used? What I mean, shouldn't we rather use the BIO_f_readbuffer internally in libcrypto or providers than requiring the app changes?

> I am still concerned about one thing - this technically is an API break, isn't it? Or do the BIO APIs that read keys and certs that were present in 1.1.1 work still with unseekable BIOs without the BIO_f_readbuffer used?

This is actually a good point. I think the seeking requirement comes from the decoders - but a number of the old style APIs "wrap" the decoders, so I suspect there could be an API break there??

How often are people going to be piping from stdin in their app??
Wouldnt this just be the OSSL_DECODER_from_bio() which is mainly used by the file_store via OSSL_STORE_attach..
PEM_read_bio_PUBKEY_ex() for example uses this.
Wouldn't you then have to do something relatively nasty to traverse the input bio chain to check down to the end if stdin is down the bottom and then create a new mem bio and tack in onto the top of the chain somehow.. (and then there could be a provider bio at the top).
The decoders are doing the seeking - previous implementation did not - and that is what introduced the breakage that this approach is fixing.
And it is very common for applications to run the openssl app in a pipe - which will very much trip over this issue.

openssl app is fine with these changes..
@t8m is talking about all the other public API's that use the decoder internally.

> How often are people going to be piping from stdin in their app??
> Wouldnt this just be the OSSL_DECODER_from_bio() which is mainly used by the file_store via OSSL_STORE_attach..
> PEM_read_bio_PUBKEY_ex() for example uses this.
> Wouldn't you then have to do something relatively nasty to traverse the input bio chain to check down to the end if stdin is down the bottom and then create a new mem bio and tack in onto the top of the chain somehow.. (and then there could be a provider bio at the top).

Couldn't you just unconditionally stack the BIO_f_readbuffer on the bio you get in OSSL_DECODER_from_bio()?

Anyway, I do not think this necessarily has to be solved in this PR. But at least an issue against the beta1 should be raised and OTC should discuss it.

But perhaps also splitting the commit to separate the addition of the BIO_f_readbuffer() and its use in the apps would help possible later fixes.

> Couldn't you just unconditionally stack the BIO_f_readbuffer on the bio you get in OSSL_DECODER_from_bio()?

It turns out that this looks like the correct place to temporarily push the new bio if required..
I only add it in the case where ftell doesnt work - if we want to add it all the time it gets a bit trickier as we would need to check for mem bio's that are in the chain already. I think the conditional approach is sufficient - but coulfd be changed later if someone disagrees. Either way this make the changes transparent to the app layer which is good.

For people who have already reviewed - I had to rebase this and collapse.. the new BIO code and file_store hasnt changed.
Only the decoder changed, with updates to CHANGES and the pod files.
The sanitizer issue is not related to this PR.. I can see it in other builds also.
@t8m thanks for the feedback!

> The decoders are doing the seeking

Er, no?  It's decoder_process(), in crypto/encoder_decoder/decoder_lib.c, that does this.

Thanks for reviewing. Merged to master.

issue_context.title: OSSL_DECODER cannot read from stdin
issue_context.body:
Using the code in #13138, I run this command:

````
$ cat dh.pem | openssl dhparam -noout -text
````
This fails with:

````
Error, unable to load parameters
80B23C65177F0000:error::DECODER routines:decoder_process:BIO lib:crypto/encode_decode/decoder_lib.c:511:
````

The problem seems to be here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/1dc5128577ed983fab8d5b3e65c06dd7e12cf4dc/crypto/encode_decode/decoder_lib.c#L510-L513

Calling `BIO_tell()` on stdin just fails immediately and we bail out at this point.
comments:
Ok, that does it.  We really need a BIO filter/source-sink that can handle this kind of stuff.  I've hinted at this here:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/1dc5128577ed983fab8d5b3e65c06dd7e12cf4dc/providers/implementations/storemgmt/file_store.c#L327-L331
Another suggestion is to use OSSL_STORE for this sort of thing.  It deals better with stdin.
Moved to 3.0.0 beta1 as this potentially requires API changes.

> Moved to 3.0.0 beta1 as this potentially requires API changes.

I don't think it will require public API changes, not the way I imagine it.  But it's definitely "work not done", so beta1 is appropriate either way.
See #13352 for another use case which fails reading am pem file from stdin via a pipe.

@levitte Do you mind if I attempt this one?

I am thinking of doing a mem_cache bio that can chain to a file bio.
It would just buffer into memory all the reads from the file bio. it can seek backwards.
ftell would be the location in the read buffer. seek would just go backwards in the buffer.
@slontis, I do not mind at all, please go ahead (you have my thanks!).  What you describe seems to be what I had in mind.
I am describing a filter here not a source/sink...

> I am describing a filter here not a source/sink...

Details...  the functionality you describe is still what I had in mind.
